title: How to Use the New Siri for Work: Emails, Notes, and Tasks
summary: Learn how to use the new Siri for work with prompts for emails, notes, and reminders. See where Siri helps and when to try VoiceOS for desktop tasks.
body_markdown:
### Is the new Siri already available to everyone?


No. Apple’s U.S. announcement schedules the Siri AI beta for September 14, 2026, on supported devices set to English. Availability varies by region and language. This article was updated September 10, before that rollout.\[1\]


### Can the new Siri write work emails?


Apple advertises composing and editing text with Siri AI, including messages. Try it with the facts and tone you want, then check the recipient and any commitments before sending. This guide does not claim a hands-on result.\[2\]


### What is a Siri alternative for work on a Mac?


VoiceOS is an option for voice writing and actions in connected work apps. Consider it when you want a dedicated desktop workflow, and compare the result on tasks you repeat. There is no universal winner for every app or user.\[4\]\[5\]


### Is Siri the same as Apple Dictation?


No. Apple Dictation enters spoken text where you can type. Siri is an assistant for requests and supported actions. On a Mac, Dictation is configured in System Settings under Keyboard.\[3\]


### Does VoiceOS replace Siri on the iPhone?


This article recommends VoiceOS for computer workflows. It does not claim that VoiceOS replaces the iPhone’s system Siri integration. Evaluate each product on the device and task where you intend to use it.


### Can VoiceOS send tasks to Codex and Claude Code?


The team-supplied screenshots in this article show a Codex research task marked Working and a separate Claude Code research task marked Queued inside VoiceOS. They demonstrate task dispatch and status tracking; they do not show the final research results.
